key_insight: LongMedBench shows that evaluating medical agents needs long-horizon, multi-visit reasoning—not just short-context QA or tool use.
clinical_relevance: A benchmark built on longitudinal EHR data can better test whether AI agents can track evolving patient history and support realistic clinical decision-making over time.
method: Built a reproducible pipeline from MIMIC-IV admission records and clinical notes
Converted EHRs into time-series event streams and long-context memory datasets
Evaluated agents across fact-based QA, temporal reasoning, and long-horizon decision-making
evidence_signal: The benchmark includes 335 patients, averaging 19.72 inpatient visits and 44.91 medical events per visit, and the abstract reports that explicit timestamps help more than implicit time inference.
watch_item: Performance on decision-making tasks appears highly sensitive to the model’s immediate context, so results may not generalize well to real longitudinal clinical workflows without careful validation.
paper_title: LongMedBench: Benchmarking Medical Agents for Long-Horizon Clinical Decision-Making
